Video Title: 25   Friday Sermon by Dr  Rashad Khalifa   Marriage    Importance of Love    Muhammad's Example
Text: Alhamdu Lillah, praise be to God
Speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
Description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa presents the Quranic law of marriage as resting on two requirements: love, which he grounds in Sura 4:24 and Sura 30:21 and says cannot exist without a real period of acquaintance, and a dowry, whose purpose he identifies as security for the wife. He extends the security argument to divorce, citing Sura 2:240-241 on alimony and Sura 65:1 on the prohibition against turning a wife out of the house, and describes the Middle Eastern practice of an official marriage followed by a long interval before consummation as one way of satisfying the first requirement. The second sermon treats self-discipline as the foundation of all religious practice, invoking Sura 7:179 on people who become worse than animals, contrasting the televangelists Jimmy Swaggart and Jim Bakker with a believer whose soul is stronger than the body, and offering his own experience at scientific conferences as illustration. He closes on polygamy, which he says the Quran permits under many conditions while Muhammad's twenty-five years with one wife and his later marriages to widows set the example, and on divorce, which he says God hates and hedges with protections for women drawn from Sura 28:5. Related recording: this sermon also appears as a sample sermon in the second half of "18 - Principles of Friday Prayer" in this collection.
